newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Davids to merge food service unit with PFD.
newsitem.headline: Davids to merge food service unit with PFD.

text.p: Grocery wholesaler Davids Ltd said on Monday it will merge its John Lewis Food Service division with Glacier Holdings (Australia) Pty Ltd-PFD Food Services to create Australia's largest food service company.
Davids said there was no cash outlay involved in the merger, which is scheduled to take place on July 1, 1997.
Davids will own 60 percent and PFD 40 percent of the joint venture, which will have sales of near A$600 million, it said.
The food service industry supplies frozen, refrigerated, dry and fresh food and ingredients to hotels, restaurants, fast food outlets and food processors.
Davids managing director Jeff David said the merger would increase purchasing power for the unit, and reduce administration costs and inventory.

John Lewis Food Service has sales of about A$400 million and PFD has sales of A$180 million. The chief executive of the joint venture, to be headquartered in Melbourne, will be Richard Smith, the owner and managing director of PFD. Davids will have the majority of directors and appoint the chairman.

PFD operates 15 warehouses in Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia and Tasmania. These will be merged with the 12 John Lewis sites in Queensland, New South Wales, South Australia, the Northern Territory and Victoria.
